principles.text: Chasing a strong gap-up is justified when you have a profit cushion: accept a lower win rate, risk only 1-2%, and aim to capture the straight-up rally — giving back 1-2% is fine if it fails.

Size new positions off real-time account value (often discounting ~10%), and keep new-trade size similar to or smaller than existing positions; smaller new size when already loaded controls drawdown and avoids amplifying losses when the market reverses.

When you have many working positions the market is likely stretched, so new entries carry a lower win rate; under-sizing new trades reduces drawdown and protects your mental capital for holding existing winners.
After a losing streak, stop trading for a day or two to reset; only re-engage for high-conviction setups and size small (~3% risk per trade) so 10 losses in a row is only a mild ~3% drawdown.
Never increase risk per trade while in a drawdown/losing streak — that was a costly 2024 mistake; if you avoid risking more when losing, you'll stay fine unless you're wildly overtrading.
Use plain market stop orders (not limit). On a premarket gap-down, wait for the open and let it execute, or wait the first 5-15 minutes for the spread to tighten before selling on market.
